कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार

अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने

4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था

New Delhi, the 29th July, 2026 


S.R.O. 26.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Navy [Group ‘C’, Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial, Non-Industrial Posts, Drawing Office and 
National Hydrographic Office (Drawing staff)] Recruitment Rules, 2003, in so far as they relate to the post of 
Draughtsman Grade-II (Armament); and the Integrated Headquarters of Ministry of Defence (Navy), Group ‘B’ 
(Draughtsman) Recruitment Rules, 2008, in so far as they relate to the post of Draughtsman Grade-I (Armament), 
except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Senior Draughtsman (Armament) in the Naval 
Headquarters, Ministry of Defence, namely :— 


. Short title and commencement.— (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Naval 
Headquarters, Senior Draughtsman (Armament), Group ‘B’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.— The number of the said post, its classification 
and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualification — No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-

Lieutenant Colonel Maneo Francis PF, SC, the Assault Team Commander of a Parachute Regiment (Special Forces), 
swiftly established a highly coordinated intelligence network to systematically dismantle anti-national elements fueling 
violence and division in Manipur.

On 23 Mar 25, based on inputs from local villagers regarding the presence of heavily armed foreign terrorists in the 
forested region near the International Border in Jammu's Samba district, a joint operation by J&K Police and other security 
forces was promptly launched. Despite the terrorists initially evading contact under the cover of night, determined efforts by 
the teams, led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch, SDPO Border, and Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, SHO Police Station Rajbagh, supported 
by ground intelligence and tireless tracking, narrowed their escape trail into the rugged Bani-Basholi-Billawar belt. On the 
intervening night of 26/27 Mar 25, continuous search operation and human intelligence pinpointed the terrorists’ likely presence 
in the thickly forested villages of Soffain and Jothana. Multiple ambushes were laid at strategic locations with meticulous 
coordination by senior officers. Teams led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch and Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, comprising HC Jagbir 
Singh, SgCt Jaswant Singh, SgCt Tariq Hussain, and SgCt Balvinder Singh, took on the most exposed and dangerous positions 
deep within the terrain. 


At 0900 hrs on 27 Mar 25, the terrorists, concealed in a tactically superior position, opened indiscriminate fire. These 
terrorists were highly trained, heavily armed, and affiliated with the proscribed Pakistan-based outfit Jaish-e-Mohammad. 
Unfazed by the sudden and overwhelming onslaught, the teams specifically led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch and Insp. Ajay 
Singh Chib retaliated with resolute grit and raw courage, holding their ground under intense fire. In the ensuing fierce firefight 
and grenade exchanges, HC Jagbir Singh, SgCt Jaswant Singh, SgCt Tariq Hussain, and SgCt Balvinder Singh were grievously 
injured and later succumbed to their wounds. Their supreme sacrifice was instrumental in pinning down the terrorists and their 
elimination. Despite sustaining bullet and splinter injuries, DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch steadfastly held his position with 
extraordinary resolve, while Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, though uninjured, continued to lead his team from the front with 
unwavering composure and bravery. The cordon was further reinforced by other forces, culminating in the successful 
neutralization of two foreign terrorists and recovery of a large cache of arms and war-like stores, including an M4 rifle, 
two AK-47 rifles, grenades, %.5 lakh in Indian currency, electronic gadgets, and rations. 


For displaying unparalleled bravery, selfless devotion to duty, and raw courage in the face of certain death, Late Jagbir 
Singh, Head Constable EXJ9760l8, Late Jaswant Singh, Sg Constable EXJ00606l, Late Tariq Hussain, Sg Constable 
EXJ746l, and Late Balvinder Singh, Sg Constable EXJ007020 are awarded “KIRTI CHAKRA” (POSTHUMOUS). 


8. ARP9055l5 HEAD CONSTABLE BASHIR AHMED, J&K POLICE (POSTHUMOUS) 
(Effective date of Award: 28 September 2024) 


While following the leads received, post ambush on Army patrolling party near Badnota, in which five Army personnel 
got martyred, input was received on 28 Sep 24 at around 00 h, regarding the presence of a group of Pakistani terrorists, 
belonging to Jaish-e-Mohammad outfit, in a house in village Dhanuparole in Kathua district. It was also learned that they were 
planning to attack a polling center nearby, which was going to the polls after two days. Acting on this tip-off, a posse of police 
commandos, including DSP Sukhvir Singh, ASI Niaz Ahmad & HC Bashir Ahmad, and contingents of Army & CRPF, 
launched a joint cordon and search operation. 


The team split into two groups; one was led by DSP Sukhvir Singh, and the other included ASI Niaz Ahmad and HC 
Bashir Ahmad, among others. After keeping the house under surveillance for about six hours, the first team in the evening 
hours, observed some suspicious activities inside it, on which they decided to zero in and conduct a thorough search, while the 
other team placed a stop on the escape route. As the team started heading to the suspected house, sensing danger, terrorists 
suddenly came out and, in an attempt, to flee from the spot, they resorted to indiscriminate firing on the joint search team. 
However, HC Bashir Ahmad, who was holding a Light Machine Gun, pinned them down and forced them to retreat. Realizing 
the fact that HC Bashir Ahmad was the main hindrance, they pin-pointedly targeted him with their sophisticated weapons like 
M-4, leaving him critically injured. As the rest of the members tried to evacuate him, terrorists got an opportunity to slip away, 
which was resisted by DSP Sukhvir Singh and ASI Niaz Ahmad, who also sustained firearm injuries. However, taking benefit 
of darkness and rugged terrain, four terrorists fled away from the encounter site. Later, on the search of the scene of the 
encounter, including the house, one dead body of a dreaded foreign terrorist besides war-like stores was recovered. All the 
three injured policemen were evacuated, however, HC Bashir Ahmad, who was critically injured, succumbed en route. 


For exhibiting exemplary courage in the face of death, beyond the call of duty and upholding the highest traditions of 
bravery and sacrifice, Late Bashir Ahmed, Head Constable ARP90555 is awarded “KIRTI CHAKRA” (POSTHUMOUS).

duty during the operation. 


For his act of bravery in the face of enemy, Lance Naik Kapil Dev is awarded “SHAURYA CHAKRA”. 
. 4498758L SEPOY JASWINDER SINGH, 7th BATTALION THE SIKH LIGHT INFANTRY 
(Effective date of Award: 23 January 2026) 


Sepoy Jaswinder Singh demonstrated raw courage and mettle in eliminating armed foreign terrorist during high risk 
house intervention operation in remote village of Kathua district. 


PART [-.86०. | THE GAZETTE OF INDIA, OCTOBER 3, 2026 (ASVINA I], 948) 443 


On 23 January 2026, despite heavy rainfall Sepoy Jaswinder Singh led an assault team with tactical audacity and 
excellent battle craft through dense foliage, approaching the target house with surprise. He ensured visual contact with support 
team and obtained positive confirmation of no civilian presence inside house. With utter disregard to personal safety, he led 
the deliberate search of house through alternate entry. He correctly appreciated presence of terrorist with weapon inside kitchen. 
Realizing grave danger to his team, Sepoy Jaswinder Singh swiftly dashed towards the terrorist and neutralised him with 
effective fire from personal weapon in close encounter. His presence of mind and sheer grit denied any reaction time to terrorist, 
thereby concluding the operation in merely few minutes. 


The daring act by Sepoy Jaswinder led to neutralisation of one drafed terrorist responsible for numerous terrorist 
incidents in Kathua district since 2024 and recover of M-4 Assault Rifles including other warlike stores. 


For conspicuous bravery, fearlessness and daring in eliminating a foreign terrorist, Sepoy Jaswinder Singh is awarded 
“SHAURYA CHAKRA”. 


2. 09-Y LIEUTENANT COMMANDER SHIVAM KUMAR 
(Effective date of Award: 8 October 2025) 


Lieutenant Commander Shivam Kumar, serving as the NBCD Officer onboard INS Trikand, displayed exceptional 
courage and gallantry during Operation Sanchet in the Gulf of Aden on 8 October 2025. INS Trikand was directed to render 
immediate assistance to MT Falcon, a Cameroon-flagged LPG tanker that had suffered a catastrophic explosion and major fire 
in the Houthi Attack Zone. The structurally damaged vessel was adrift, with an uncontrolled fire continuously fuelled by leaking 
LPG, creating an imminent risk of a devastating secondary explosion. Two Indian crew members were missing and presumed 
trapped onboard. 


Fully aware of the extreme danger posed by explosive LPG vapours, toxic smoke, intense heat, oxygen-deficient 
compartments, weakened structures and the possibility of hostile action, Lieutenant Commander Shivam Kumar voluntarily 
led the high-risk operation. He repeatedly entered the burning and gas-filled compartments, conducting dynamic technical and 
risk assessments and guiding his team through severely damaged and smoke-filled spaces. 


Displaying remarkable composure, professional competence and complete disregard for personal safety, he 
spearheaded repeated internal searches for the missing crew members. Despite prolonged exposure to toxic gases, extreme 
heat, physical exhaustion and intense psychological stress, he personally supervised and participated in the recovery of the 
dismembered and decomposed mortal remains from damaged compartments, ensuring their safe and dignified retrieval. 


His fearless leadership and most conspicuous gallantry were instrumental in the successful completion of this 
extraordinarily hazardous operation, bringing immense credit while significantly enhancing the image of the Indian Navy as a 
resolute, capable and dependable maritime force. For his successful conduct of an extraordinarily hazardous rescue, Lieutenant 
Commander Shivam Kumar is awarded SHAURYA CHAKRA. 


3. 34544, SQUADRON LEADER SUDHIR KUMAR, FLYING (PILOT) 
(Effective date of Award: 09 September 2025) 


On 09 September 2025, he was authorised to fly as captain of ac for a low-flying and low-level navigation sortie by 
night from the rear cockpit of the Su-30 MK] aircraft, accompanied by an Under Training (U/T) pilot in the front cockpit. 
During the recovery phase, at an altitude of 2.2 km and a speed of 740 kmph, the aircraft experienced a catastrophic failure that 
manifested as violent oscillations in the longitudinal plane accompanied by multiple indicators of Fly By Wire (FBW) system 
failure. This critical situation resulted in drastic pitch variations ranging from +45 degrees to -l5 degrees, extreme g-loads 
spanning from -l.5 g to +l2 g along with Angle of Attack (AOA) indications exceeding 24 units. As the supervisor in the 
cockpit he demonstrated exceptional situational awareness and airmanship despite experiencing physical forces that exceeded 
normative limits for human tolerance. Under extreme conditions of rapidly varying g-loads and pitch, he maintained a 
composed and calm demeanour, swiftly taking control of the situation and instructing the front pilot to reset the failed FBW 
channels. He exercised exemplary judgment by first corroborating that the critical FBW red light was not illuminated before 
guiding the front pilot to operate the correct switches. 


The ensuing task was extremely demanding given the violent onset of intense g-forces and the rapidity of the 
manoeuvre that manifested under conditions of total darkness by night. Without any external frame of reference and unable to 
discern the aircraft instruments due to blurring of vision, he demonstrated extraordinary airmanship and praiseworthy intuition 
by promptly re-opening power on the aircraft. This prevented a potentially cataclysmic accident that could have occurred due 
to rapid loss of airspeed. Throughout the emergency he displayed absolute professionalism and composure, and maintained apt 
responsiveness despite being in extreme physical agony while struggling to stay conscious and remain oriented. Furthermore, 
he demonstrated outstanding leadership and supervisory acumen by guiding and reassuring the U/T pilot in the front cockpit. 
These gallant actions highlight exceptional bravery in taking precise and correct measures under extreme pressure.

For this act of gallantry, Squadron Leader Sudhir Kumar is awarded ‘SHAURYA CHAKRA’. 
4. JKPSI25836 DEPUTY SUPERINTENDENT OF POLICE DHERAJ SINGH KATOCH, J&K POLICE 
5. EXJ006226 INSPECTOR AJAY SINGH CHIB, J&K POLICE 
(Effective date of Award: 23 March 2025) 


On 23 Mar 25, based on inputs from local villagers regarding the presence of heavily armed foreign terrorists in the 
forested region near the International Border in Jammu's Samba district, a joint operation by J&K Police and other security 
forces was promptly launched. Despite the terrorists initially evading contact under the cover of night, determined efforts by 
the teams, led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch, SDPO Border, and Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, SHO Police Station Rajbagh, supported 
by ground intelligence and tireless tracking, narrowed their escape trail into the rugged Bani-Basholi-Billawar belt. On the 
intervening night of 26/27 Mar 25, continuous search operation and human intelligence pinpointed the terrorists’ likely presence 
in the thickly forested villages of Soffain and Jothana. Multiple ambushes were laid at strategic locations with meticulous 
coordination by senior officers. Teams led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch and Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, comprising HC Jagbir 
Singh, SgCt Jaswant Singh, SgCt Tariq Hussain, and SgCt Balvinder Singh, took on the most exposed and dangerous positions 
deep within the terrain. 


At 0900 hrs on 27 Mar 25, the terrorists, concealed in a tactically superior position, opened indiscriminate fire. These 
terrorists were highly trained, heavily armed, and affiliated with the proscribed Pakistan-based outfit Jaish-e-Mohammad. 
Unfazed by the sudden and overwhelming onslaught, the teams specifically led by DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch and Insp. Ajay 
Singh Chib retaliated with resolute grit and raw courage, holding their ground under intense fire. In the ensuing fierce firefight 
and grenade exchanges, HC Jagbir Singh, SgCt Jaswant Singh, SgCt Tariq Hussain, and SgCt Balvinder Singh were grievously 
injured and later succumbed to their wounds. Their supreme sacrifice was instrumental in pinning down the terrorists and their 
elimination. Despite sustaining bullet and splinter injuries, DSP Dheraj Singh Katoch steadfastly held his position with 
extraordinary resolve, while Insp. Ajay Singh Chib, though uninjured, continued to lead his team from the front with 
unwavering composure and bravery. The cordon was further reinforced by other forces, culminating in the successful 
neutralization of two foreign terrorists and recovery of a large cache of arms and war-like stores, including an M4 rifle, two 
AK-47 rifles, grenades, रें.5 lakh in Indian currency, electronic gadgets, and rations. 


For their fearless leadership, conspicuous gallantry, and vital contribution to the success of the operation Dheraj Singh 
Katoch, Deputy Superintendent of Police JKPS25836 and Ajay Singh Chib, Inspector EXJ006226 are awarded “SHAURYA 
CHAKRA”. 


6. ARP98556l DEPUTY SUPERINDENTENT OF POLICE SUKHVIR SINGH, J&K POLICE 
7. EXJ98633 ASSISTANT SUB INSPECTOR NIAZ AHMED, J&K POLICE 
(Effective date of Award: 28 September 2024) 


While following the leads received, post ambush on Army patrolling party near Badnota, in which five Army 
personnel got martyred, input was received on 28 Sep 24 at around !00 h, regarding the presence of a group of Pakistani 
terrorists, belonging to Jaish-e-Mohammad outfit, in a house in village Dhanuparole in Kathua district. It was also learned that 
they were planning to attack a polling center nearby, which was going to the polls after two days. Acting on this tip-off, a posse 
of police commandos, including DSP Sukhvir Singh, ASI Niaz Ahmad & HC Bashir Ahmad, and contingents of Army & 
CRPF, launched a joint cordon and search operation. 


The team split into two groups; one was led by DSP Sukhvir Singh, and the other included ASI Niaz Ahmad and HC 
Bashir Ahmad, among others. After keeping the house under surveillance for about six hours, the first team in the evening 
hours, observed some suspicious activities inside it, on which they decided to zero in and conduct a thorough search, while the 
other team placed a stop on the escape route. As the team started heading to the suspected house, sensing danger, terrorists 
suddenly came out and, in an attempt, to flee from the spot, they resorted to indiscriminate firing on the joint search team. 
However, HC Bashir Ahmad, who was holding a Light Machine Gun, pinned them down and forced them to retreat. Realizing 
the fact that HC Bashir Ahmad was the main hindrance, they pin-pointedly targeted him with their sophisticated weapons like 
M-4, leaving him critically injured. As the rest of the members tried to evacuate him, terrorists got an opportunity to slip away, 
which was resisted by DSP Sukhvir Singh and ASI Niaz Ahmad, who also sustained firearm injuries. However, taking benefit 
of darkness and rugged terrain, four terrorists fled away from the encounter site. Later, on the search of the scene of the 
encounter, including the house, one dead body of a dreaded foreign terrorist besides war-like stores was recovered. All the 
three injured policemen were evacuated, however, HC Bashir Ahmad, who was critically injured, succumbed en route. 


For exhibiting exemplary courage in the face of death, beyond the call of duty and upholding the highest traditions of 
bravery and sacrifice Sukhvir Singh, Deputy Superintendent of Police ARP98556l & Niaz Ahmed, Assitant Sub Inspector 
(Now Sub Inspector) EXJ98633 are awarded “SHAURYA CHAKRA”.

8. 75939 DEPUTY COMMANDANT ANJANI KUMAR, 209 CoBRA, CRPF 
(Effective date of Award: 20 April 2025) 


Sh. Anjani Kumar, Deputy Commandant, played a pivotal role in the unprecedented success of operation Dakabeda, 
conducted in the Luguburu forest area in Distt Bokaro, Jharkhand. His exemplary leadership, strategic insight and display of 
courage under fire were evident throughout the encounter, which was conducted in extremely challenging terrain and under 
constant threat from heavily armed Naxals, ambushes, landmines and IEDs. 


As his strike party approached the suspected target area, they came under a deadly attack from Naxals positioned on 
fortified ground. Undeterred, Sh Anjani Kumar, DC and his buddy displayed tactical brilliance, retaliating with precision. 
Crawling through intense gunfire, they reached the enemy positions, neutralizing a Naxal who was targeting the team. Their 
gallant actions caused the remaining Naxals to flee from their positions. 


During the gun fight, while chasing the fleeing naxals, Ct/GD Laljith V. of strike team was dangerously exposed in 
an open patch as his personal weapon got stoppages. Sh Anjani Kumar, DC risked his life and ordered his buddy Ct/GD Dipak 
Sah to give cover fire and crawled under fire and saved his colleague. Multiple exchanges of fire ensued as the strike party 
chased the fleeing Naxals, with bullets flying all around. Amidst these life-threatening circumstances, Sh. Anjani Kumar, DC 
remained composed, making critical decisions and maintaining team coordination. 


In a particularly perilous encounter, Sh Anjani Kumar, DC and his buddy engaged a Naxal hiding in a cave, 
neutralizing him in close combat. Even after their commander was neutralized, the Naxals launched a fierce counterattack. Sh 
Anjani Kumar, DC continued to inspire his team, ultimately neutralizing a third Naxal with targeted fire. 


Throughout the operation, Sh Anjani Kumar, DC demonstrated outstanding strategic acumen, effective leadership and 
unmatched bravery. His actions resulted in the elimination of three key Naxals, including one CCM and one SZCM and greatly 
contributed to the overall outcome. During this operation, eight Naxals got neutralized, one captured alive and fourteen weapons 
recovered. The achievement without any casualties to his team indicated extra-ordinary tactical acumen ship and calibrated 
strike. 


For his stout leadership, extraordinary courage and indomitable valour under extreme adversity, Sh. Anjani Kumar, 
Deputy Commandant of 209 CoBRA, is awarded "SHAURYA CHAKRA". 


9. [75322662 CONSTABLE DIPAK SAH, 209 CoBRA, CRPF 
(Effective date of Award: 20 April 2025) 


Ct/GD Dipak Sah played a crucial role in operation Dakabeda, conducted in the Luguburu forest area in Distt Bokaro, 
Jharkhand, as a key member of the strike party and buddy to the operation commander Shri Anjani Kumar Deputy 
Commandant. During a fierce gun battle, Ct/(GD Dipak Sah and his commander neutralized three Naxals, significantly 
contributing to the operation's success. 


As the strike party approached the suspected target area, hidden Naxals initiated indiscriminate firing. On his 
commander's orders, Ct/GD Dipak Sah advanced bravely from the left flank, retaliated heavily, and reached the Naxal positions 
with his buddy. Demonstrating remarkable gallantry, he neutralized a Naxal, firing from a position behind a tree. The remaining 
Naxals retreated, firing sporadically as they fled. 

While pursuing the fleeing adversaries, Ct/GD Laljit V. became vulnerable in open ground as his personal weapon 
developed stoppages. Without any hesitation, Ct/GD Dipak Sah, exemplifying camaraderie, crawled forward with his buddy 
to provide covering fire and support, ensuring his teammate's safety. 

Continuing the assault, Ct/GD Dipak Sah advanced into the centre of the cordon, facing a barrage of bullets from 
Naxals concealed in boulders and a cave. He and his buddy used fire and move tactics to close in on the enemy, ultimately 
neutralizing the Naxal commander in a close-quarters encounter. Despite escalating attacks, the duo fiercely continued 
retaliation, and through a coordinated assault, eliminated a third Naxal, thereby demonstrating unwavering courage and 
operational commitment. 


For his extraordinary bravery, indomitable spirit and devotion to duty under life-threatening circumstances, Ct/GD 
Dipak Sah of 209 CoBRA is awarded "SHAURYA CHAKRA".
